title: Keeping the back room usable
target: How the back room works in Supermarket Simulator: storage as sections rather than one pile, the tab that shows it, the cells you can sort, crates as objects with a grid of their own, the manager and door behind the sections, and the storage upgrade you have to buy.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop that is open with a back room in use
At least one crate or delivery to store
Enough money for the storage upgrade if you are expanding

steps.do: Think of the back room as sections rather than as one pile.
steps.because: storage is laid out in sections with a defined arrangement, so what you own is grouped rather than spread over one shelf (StorageSectionItem, StorageLayoutConfig)

steps.do: Look at what you have through the storage tab rather than by walking about.
steps.because: storage has its own interface tab, so the state of the back room can be read from the same place you manage the rest of the shop (StorageTab)

steps.do: Sort the cells before the section is full, not after.
steps.because: storage cells can be sorted, which is what keeps a section searchable as it fills (SortableAreaCell)

steps.do: Buy crates knowing they are objects you then place.
steps.because: a crate is an object of its own and is also sold as an item, so buying one is not the same as having somewhere for it (Crate, CrateSaleItem)

steps.do: In a shared shop, expect the crate you move to move for everyone.
steps.because: a crate has an interaction of its own and a networked version of it, so handling one is a shared event (CrateInteraction, NetworkCrateInteraction)

steps.do: Do not treat a crate as a bin with no order.
steps.because: the game keeps a grid of numbers for a crate, which is why what is in one is arranged rather than tipped in (CrateGridNumbersAuto)

steps.do: Expect the sections to be a system of their own behind their own door.
steps.because: the sections are managed by their own manager with their own data and a door of their own, so the back room is a place in the shop and not only a list (StorageSectionManager, StorageSO, StorageDoor)

steps.do: Do not expect storage to grow by itself.
steps.because: storage has its own upgrade level and a purchase behind it, so more room is bought rather than unlocked by time (storageUpgradeLevel, purchasedStorage)

steps.do: Expect growth to be presented through the same sections.
steps.because: growth is shown in sections too, so expanding the shop uses the arrangement you already know rather than a new screen (GrowthSectionItem)

steps.do: Buy a crate with a home in mind.
steps.because: what you buy becomes an object in the shop, so a delivery with nowhere to go is a problem you made rather than one the game made for you (Crate, StorageSectionItem)

commonMistakes: Treating storage as one flat list and losing track of what is where.
Filling a section until nothing in it can be found.
Buying crates with no space set aside for them.
Expecting storage space to grow without buying the upgrade.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
